09_pred_vs_actual_stress: Predicted versus analytical maximum bending stress on the held-out test set (N = 4500, log-log axes). Points on the dashed line are perfect predictions.
10_pred_vs_actual_deflection: Predicted versus analytical maximum tip deflection on the held-out test set (N = 4500, log-log axes).
11_residuals: Relative residuals versus the analytical value for stress (top) and tip deflection (bottom) on the test set (axis clipped at +/-40 %). Tree ensembles show larger, heteroscedastic errors at the extremes of the target range, where training data are sparse; the MLP residuals are small and nearly unbiased.
12_model_comparison: Test-set comparison of all regression models (log scale). 1 - R^2 is shown so that differences between near-perfect models remain visible. 'MLP (raw inputs)' is an ablation without the log10 input transform. The power-law (log-OLS) baseline is omitted because it is exact to machine precision (errors ~1e-12 %), the analytical model being a product of powers of the inputs.
13_confusion_matrices: Confusion matrices for yield classification on the test set (N = 4500). The first three panels are direct classifiers trained on the six inputs; the last panel thresholds the FoS implied by the best stress regressor (FoS = sigma_y / sigma_pred < 1).
14_fos_misclassification: Rate at which the regression-derived yield classification is wrong, binned by the true factor of safety. Errors concentrate in a narrow band around FoS = 1, where a small relative stress error flips the class; beams far from the yield boundary are always classified correctly.
15_extrapolation_force: Out-of-distribution test: models retrained only on beams with F <= 6574 N and evaluated on larger forces. Tree ensembles cannot predict outside the range of training targets (piecewise-constant extrapolation), so their stress predictions saturate and the error grows with F; the MLP on log inputs extrapolates far better because the log-space mapping is nearly linear.
16_sensitivity_sweeps: One-at-a-time sensitivity sweeps about the baseline beam (L = 1 m, b = 50 mm, h = 40 mm, F = 2 kN, E = 200 GPa, sigma_y = 250 MPa). Black: analytical solution; coloured: ML predictions. Grey bands mark parts of the sweep excluded from the training data (validity constraints), where the models extrapolate.
17_elasticity_comparison: Elasticities (log-log slopes) recovered from each model along the OAT sweeps (valid domain only) compared with the exact exponents of sigma = 6FL/(bh^2), delta = 4FL^3/(Ebh^3) and FoS = sigma_y/sigma.
18_global_variance_shares: Global sensitivity over the dataset: share of the variance of log10(response) attributable to each input, computed with the covariance decomposition S_i = a_i Cov(log10 x_i, log10 y) / Var(log10 y), where a_i are the exact exponents. The shares sum to 1 and remain valid although rejection sampling correlates the inputs.
01_feature_distributions: Distributions of the six input parameters after rejection sampling (N = 30000). Dotted lines mark the uniform sampling bounds. Non-uniform shapes (e.g. fewer thin beams, more thick/wide beams) are caused by the physical-validity constraints (slenderness, small deflection, stress <= 3 sigma_y).
02_target_distributions: Distributions of the analytical response quantities on logarithmic axes. Stress and deflection span two to three orders of magnitude, motivating the log10 target transform used for training. 19.0 % of samples exceed the yield criterion (FoS < 1).
03_correlation_heatmap: Pearson (linear) and Spearman (rank) correlation matrices of inputs and responses. Inputs are weakly correlated with each other only through the rejection-sampling constraints. Force and length correlate positively with stress; thickness negatively, consistent with sigma = 6FL/(bh^2).
04_feature_relationships: Marginal relationships between selected inputs and responses (3,000 random samples, colour = yield class). The large scatter at fixed input value shows that each response depends jointly on several parameters.
05_outlier_boxplots: Box plots of log10-transformed responses. IQR-rule outlier counts: max = 763, tip = 685, max = 836, FoS = 642. These are genuine extreme-but-valid beams, not data errors, and were retained.
06_beam_diagram: Problem definition: prismatic cantilever of length L with rectangular b x h cross-section, clamped at x = 0 and loaded by a transverse point force F at the free end. Maximum bending moment M = FL occurs at the support; maximum deflection at the tip.
07_bending_stress_field: Analytical stress and displacement fields for the baseline beam (L = 1.0 m, b = 50 mm, h = 40 mm, F = 2000 N, E = 200 GPa, sigma_y = 250 MPa). Peak |sigma| = 150 MPa at the outer fibres of the support (FoS = 1.67); the dashed contour, where present, would mark |sigma| = sigma_y. Linear variation through the thickness and along the length follows directly from M(x) = F(L - x). These are closed-form beam-theory fields, not finite-element results.
08_fos_safety_map: Factor-of-safety map over applied force and thickness with the other parameters fixed at baseline. The solid black curve is the analytical yield boundary FoS = 1 (h = sqrt(6FL/(b sigma_y))); coloured curves are the boundaries implied by each ML stress model. Hatched area: combinations excluded from the training data by the validity constraints, where ML predictions are extrapolations.
